proposals.impact: reduce intro-page abandonment before first question
proposals.observation: The quiz recorded one session in the last 48 hours. That session loaded the intro page and stopped. Zero starts, zero completions. The furthest-step distribution shows every visitor dropped at intro_load, meaning something on the intro screen killed intent before the first question appeared. This is the entire top of the funnel. One lost session is a small number, but a 0% start rate means the intro page is doing no persuasive work at all.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the quiz intro CTA block. The current text almost certainly relies on generic benefit-promise language ("find out your money personality", "get your results") that gives a 25-35 year-old earner no reason to believe the next four minutes will be different from any other quiz they've clicked away from. Replace it with copy grounded in the specific tension Joel's ICP actually carries: earning well, spending freely, and still not being able to show for it. Make the ask feel like quiet honesty rather than a personality-test hook. No promises about what the quiz will "reveal" or "unlock" — frame it as a chance to name something the person already half-knows but hasn't said out loud.
proposals.current_text: Find out your money personality in under 4 minutes. Answer honestly and get a personalised breakdown of the beliefs driving your financial behaviour.
proposals.new_text:
You probably already have a sense of what's going on with your money. This takes under four minutes and puts words to it. No score to optimise for. No right answers. Just an honest look at how you actually relate to money — not how you think you should.

Joel Thomas, MSc Behavioural Economics | Qualified Financial Planner

proposals.impact: lift open rate on lower-performing sequences toward Vigilance benchmark
proposals.observation: The Money Vigilance automation has a 66.67% open rate across 12 sends. Money Avoidance sits at 52.63% across 19 sends. Money Worship sits at 37.5% across 16 sends. The Worship sequence is underperforming by roughly 29 percentage points compared to Vigilance. Subject line is the single controllable variable Fred can touch in one file edit that directly drives open rate. If the Worship subject line reads like a generic personality-type label, it will lose to an inbox full of noise.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line of email 1 in the Money Worship sequence. The Vigilance sequence likely earns its open rate because the Vigilance label carries a built-in tension people recognise in themselves (careful to the point of paralysis). Worship needs a subject line that does the same work: surfaces the specific, slightly uncomfortable truth that someone who scores Worship already suspects about themselves. Avoid any frame that sounds aspirational or celebratory. The reader who scores Money Worship earns and spends in ways that feel like proof of worth — the subject line should name that friction, not the personality type.
proposals.new_text: Subject: When spending feels like proof you've made it

proposals.impact: restore daily content publishing after three consecutive failures
proposals.observation: Three workflow failures in the last 24 hours: Daily Blog Post (04:00), Funnel-Hack Digest (09:04), Weekly Queue Topup (17:55). The content queue shows only one post queued against 47 published. With Daily Blog Post failing and only one post in reserve, the publishing pipeline is one more failure away from going dark. The queue being near-empty compounds the workflow failure because there is no buffer to fall back on. This is an infrastructure problem, not a content problem, but the effect is a content gap.
proposals.proposal: Add a failure notification step to the Daily Blog Post workflow so Joel receives an email alert when the run fails, rather than discovering the gap in hindsight via Fred's daily report. The existing workflow file presumably has no on-failure notification configured, which is why three consecutive failures went unactioned for hours. A single additional step using the existing MailerLite sender or a GitHub Actions email action costs nothing and means Joel can manually publish or queue from his phone the same morning a failure occurs.
proposals.new_text:
- name: Notify on failure
        if: failure()
        uses: dawidd6/action-send-mail@v3
        with:
          server_address: smtp.mailersend.net
          server_port: 587
          username: ${{ secrets.SMTP_USERNAME }}
          password: ${{ secrets.SMTP_PASSWORD }}
          subject: "Way of Wealth: Daily Blog Post workflow failed ${{ github.run_id }}"
          to: joel@wayofwealth.co.uk
          from: fred@wayofwealth.co.uk
          body: |
            The Daily Blog Post workflow failed at ${{ github.run_id }}.
            Check the Actions tab: https://github.com/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
            Content queue has 1 post remaining. Manual publish may be needed today.
